shorts.title: Two Cups at Nine
shorts.covers: Every evening at nine an old woman, Mrs Kapoor, sets two cups of tea, and a kind 'neighbour' visits and drinks one. PLANT: the visitor always knows where the sugar is kept without asking. TWIST: Mrs Kapoor has dementia; the 'neighbour' is her daughter, who stopped correcting her months ago and simply comes every night to have tea with her mother.

shorts.title: The Last Voicemail
shorts.covers: A widower in Leeds rings his late wife's mobile every Sunday to hear her voicemail greeting, and leaves a message about his week. One Sunday a teenage girl answers. PLANT: the phone company had told him the number would be cancelled, yet it never was. TWIST: the number was reissued to the girl; she has kept every one of his messages, because they got her through the year her own mother died, and she has been paying to keep the voicemail on. She asks him not to stop calling.

shorts.title: The Reference Letter
shorts.covers: Priya is called into her boss's office and told her job is ending on Friday. The same afternoon he asks her, oddly, which company she has always dreamed of working for. PLANT: his question, and the closed door of the meeting room booked under another firm's name. TWIST: he is selling the business and the buyer will close her department; the letter he wrote that afternoon is a glowing reference, already sent to the company she named, which has offered her an interview.

shorts.title: Lost and Found
shorts.covers: Arjun loses his wallet on the Delhi metro and it comes back by post a week later, with every card in it and two thousand rupees more than he had. PLANT: the note inside calls him by a childhood nickname. TWIST: the finder is his father, who walked out twenty years ago, recognised his son's name on the cards, and could not think of any other way to give him something.

shorts.title: One Samosa, Every Day
shorts.covers: A delivery rider is sent to the same flat every day for a single samosa, and the old man always pays in coins so the rider has to wait while he counts. PLANT: one day the old man says, 'Your father hums like that too.' TWIST: the old man is the rider's grandfather, estranged from his son for decades, who found the boy's job through a relative and ordered every day just to see him.

shorts.title: The Interview
shorts.covers: Rohan nails a job interview, but the woman leading the panel is cold to him throughout. PLANT: she asks one off-script question: 'Do you remember your school?' TWIST: she is the girl he bullied for two years at school; he remembers in the lift. The next morning the job offer arrives, signed by her, with one line: 'People change. Prove it.'

shorts.title: Second Opinion
shorts.covers: An older couple each hide a hospital appointment from the other, and each makes an excuse to be out on Tuesday morning. PLANT: the receptionist smiles knowingly when each arrives. TWIST: they have the same doctor, who has been booking them on the same day at the same time, hoping they would see each other in the waiting room and stop facing it alone. They do.

shorts.title: Night Bus
shorts.covers: Every night for a week, a man gets on the last bus after Leela and gets off at her stop, and she is sure she is being followed. PLANT: the driver checks his mirror twice whenever she gets on. TWIST: the man is the driver's son, sent to walk behind her to her door, because the driver had noticed another passenger following her for days and that passenger has now stopped coming.

shorts.title: The Will Reading
shorts.covers: Three siblings hear their mother's will: the two eldest get the house money, and the youngest, Sara, who cared for her for six years, gets only a box of old letters. PLANT: their mother typed for an hour every night, 'just shopping lists.' TWIST: the letters are from a publisher; their mother was a bestselling crime writer under another name, and every future royalty goes to Sara.

shorts.title: Silent Treatment
shorts.covers: Fourteen-year-old Zoe has not said one word to her new stepfather in a year, and the house is miserable. PLANT: she spends hours in her room 'watching videos' with the sound off. TWIST: his deaf daughter from his first marriage is moving in next month; Zoe has spent the year secretly learning sign language, and her first words to him are signed.

shorts.title: The Password
shorts.covers: Nadia finds that her husband's laptop password is a date she does not recognise, and she is sure it is another woman. PLANT: he always, always offers his umbrella to strangers in the rain. TWIST: it is the date they really first met, a year before the wedding where she thinks they met, at a bus stop in the rain where he gave a stranger his umbrella and was too shy to say hello.

shorts.title: Mother's Dal
shorts.covers: After her mother's death, Meghna tries for months to recreate her famous dal and never gets it right, and the family says it is never the same. PLANT: her mother always cooked with the kitchen door shut. TWIST: in the back of the spice cupboard she finds the secret: a packet of ordinary shop-bought masala, hidden behind the jars for thirty years. She laughs for the first time since the funeral.

shorts.title: The Understudy
shorts.covers: An understudy has waited two years for one night on stage, and secretly wishes the lead would fall ill. The lead does, on opening night of the tour, and the understudy is a triumph. PLANT: the lead asks her, a week earlier, which night her parents are coming. TWIST: the lead was never ill; she gave the understudy the night her parents were in the audience, because someone once did the same for her.

shorts.title: Fourteen Missed Calls
shorts.covers: Dev comes out of a long meeting to fourteen missed calls from his father and assumes the worst about his father's heart. PLANT: his phone was not in his pocket all morning; he had been using his work phone. TWIST: his own phone was stolen; the thief's journey had shown up on the family location app at a hospital, and his father had been calling in a panic about him.

shorts.title: The Babysitter's Note
shorts.covers: Two parents come home to a note from the babysitter: 'We need to talk about Aarav.' They spend a sleepless night imagining what their six-year-old has done. PLANT: the babysitter always brings the same picture book. TWIST: the babysitter never learned to read properly, and Aarav has been teaching her, page by page; she wanted to ask if she could keep coming.

shorts.title: The Last Concert
shorts.covers: An ageing singer gives her farewell concert to a half-empty hall and walks off at the interval sure nobody cares any more. PLANT: she has been singing free every Sunday at a care home for ten years. TWIST: when the curtain goes up again every seat is full: the residents, their families and the staff of the care home, bussed in by the manager.

shorts.title: Footsteps at Three
shorts.covers: Every night at three in the morning heavy footsteps cross the flat upstairs and wake Hannah and her newborn, and she writes an angry note. PLANT: the neighbour's shoes outside the door are hospital clogs. TWIST: the neighbour is a midwife coming home from night shifts, and she is the midwife who delivered Hannah's baby.

shorts.title: Return to Sender
shorts.covers: For twenty years Leo writes to his childhood best friend, who moved abroad, and every letter comes back stamped 'return to sender'. PLANT: as boys they had a secret code where a returned letter meant something. TWIST: in their code, 'return to sender' meant 'got it, keep going'; his friend has read every letter and returned each one on purpose, and finally writes back.

shorts.title: Flowers on Thursday
shorts.covers: Months after her husband's death, a bunch of flowers arrives at Elena's door every Thursday with no card, and she suspects the kind widower across the road. PLANT: they always come on Thursdays, the day of the week her husband proposed. TWIST: her husband, knowing he was ill, prepaid a florist for a year; the last bunch, on the anniversary, comes with a card in his handwriting.

shorts.title: Stuck Between Floors
shorts.covers: Two strangers are stuck in an office lift for forty minutes; they argue, then confess their nerves, then help each other rehearse for big interviews. PLANT: both are going to floor twelve. TWIST: they are the two final candidates for the same job, and each has just coached the other.

shorts.title: The Scholarship
shorts.covers: A girl from a poor family wins an anonymous scholarship and, years later, tracks down the donor to thank him. PLANT: the donor's letters always called her by her late father's nickname for her. TWIST: the donor is her father's old business partner, whose betrayal ruined her father; this was his way of paying the debt back.

shorts.title: Where Were You on Saturday?
shorts.covers: A father catches his sixteen-year-old son lying about where he goes every Saturday and assumes the worst. PLANT: the boy comes home every Saturday smelling of hospital soap. TWIST: he has been visiting his mother, the father's ex-wife, in hospital, because he knew his father would forbid it.

shorts.title: The Fake Fiance
shorts.covers: Tired of questions, Riya hires an actor to play her fiance at her sister's wedding, and he is suspiciously good at it. PLANT: her grandmother greets him by name before Riya has introduced him. TWIST: her family knew all along; her sister had hired the same actor first, as a joke on Riya, and now cannot stop laughing.

shorts.title: The Stolen Bicycle
shorts.covers: Eleven-year-old Sam's bicycle disappears from the yard, and a week later he sees another boy riding it. PLANT: his father has been coming home late and quiet, and the rent is due. TWIST: the bike was not stolen; his father sold it to make the rent and was too ashamed to say. Sam lets the other boy keep riding.

shorts.title: Last Train Home
shorts.covers: For months a commuter talks every night on the last train to a woman with a beautiful voice, and never asks her name. One night she is not there. PLANT: she always knows the stations a few seconds before they are announced. TWIST: she was the voice of the station announcements, recorded years ago, on her way to her last day at the job; that night the announcement at his stop says his name.

shorts.title: The Promotion
shorts.covers: Two colleagues compete for one promotion and the rivalry turns bitter; Kavya wins. PLANT: her rival keeps leaving early for 'appointments'. TWIST: he recommended her for it himself; he is leaving the company to care for his father and wanted the job to go to the person who deserved it.

shorts.title: Forty Years Overdue
shorts.covers: A library book comes back forty years late with the fine paid in an envelope, and the librarian, Ruth, tracks down the borrower. PLANT: the book is a guide to the city Ruth was born in. TWIST: the borrower was Ruth's own mother, who took the book the day she left the family; the envelope holds a letter addressed to Ruth.

shorts.title: The Envelope Every Month
shorts.covers: A cafe owner finds an envelope of cash under the door every month for a year, with no name. PLANT: the cafe till was once robbed by a boy who worked there. TWIST: the money is from that boy, now grown, paying it back; the owner knew it was him the whole time, never told the police, and finally leaves an envelope of his own: a job offer.

shorts.title: The Wrong Number
shorts.covers: A nurse on a night shift keeps getting texts meant for someone else: a stranger's messages to a daughter who never replies. She starts answering gently, as if she were the daughter. PLANT: the stranger mentions a ward number, the nurse's own ward. TWIST: the stranger is a patient on her ward, dying, texting an old number; the nurse finds the real daughter in time.

shorts.title: The Bench by the Sea
shorts.covers: The council plans to remove an old bench on the seafront, and an old man sits on it every day in protest. PLANT: he always sits on the left half. TWIST: it is not a memorial to a dead wife, as everyone assumes; his wife is alive and sits on the right half each evening after work, and the bench is where they met fifty years ago. They both turn up to the council meeting.
